stage1.impression: The fir-lined niche with the pair of speakers on plinths is a clear, symmetrical subject, but the frame reads as CG. The speakers are blown to near-white, so the smoked acrylic, the horn and the batts all read as grey plastic. The fir boards look stamped and uniform, the tub chairs look like smooth salmon clay, and a hard orange-sepia cast flattens everything. The Orb lamps are flat white discs, and the right chair back is a big bright slab that pulls the eye away from the altar. A magazine would see a generic CG listening nook, not a specific place.

blocking_9: The speakers read as tinted cast acrylic with the light passing through it. The cabinets should not be blown: region [365,340,465,480] lum_median 90-150, with visible rim glow and the smoke tint holding.
The foreground chairs read as velvet with a soft sheen and do not outshine the altar. The right chair back [670,570,945,800] should sit below the speaker's median.
The fir shows real grain variation, checks and board-to-board tone differences, with no repeated plank pattern.
The grade is warm but not sepia. Concrete and fir separate in hue, and the frame median is 24-40.
The Orb lamps show their tinted shell and frosted liner instead of a white disc.
There is a visible sign of life in the zone (a glass, a record out of its sleeve) that reads at a glance.
To be read as a specific place rather than a generic bar, the frame needs at least one signature element of the room (the concrete shell, a steel beam or the record wall) at the edges.

defects.what: Speaker cabinet overexposed (median 191). The white batts and the face read as flat white-grey plastic, and the smoke tint is lost.
Same blowout on the right speaker.
The horn reads as a black blob with smeared, wobbly white reflections (denoiser smear). It does not read as a resin horn.
The right tub chair back is a flat salmon-pink slab (median 139, r190 g129 b98), brighter than the room and with no velvet texture or sheen.
The left tub chair is smooth and featureless, like clay with no nap.
The Orb lamp is a flat white disc (median 234, p95 251). There is no tint or liner structure.
The second Orb is the same flat white disc, cut by the frame edge.
The fir boards are uniform and repetitive, with no checks, nail holes or tone variation. The overall cast is heavy orange (r58 g33 b21).
A bright pale sliver at the left edge (median 119), likely a screen, distracts at the frame edge.
The sleeve against the right plinth reads as a plain beige box.
The plinth top clips under the altar spot (clip 0.61 %).
Frame median 19.9, below the 22 floor. The bottom third is dominated by chair backs.
